item.title: Wrist & Hand — Deep Transverse Friction
clinicalUse: Use when assessment identifies a relevant impairment in Wrist & Hand and the parent technique fits the patient's presentation.
Primary treatment target: wrist/hand range, grip, dexterity and task-related pain.
Retain the technique only if it produces a meaningful within-session improvement.
patientPosition: Sitting with forearm and hand supported on the table.
Keep fingers relaxed unless active movement is part of the technique.
therapistPosition: Sit or stand beside the hand so small contacts can be controlled precisely.
stabilization: Stabilize the forearm or adjacent carpal/metacarpal segment.
contact: Use small, broad contacts over the intended joint/tendon/muscle and avoid compressing superficial nerves or inflamed structures.
Identify a specific symptomatic tendon, ligament or muscle structure rather than rubbing a broad area.
Move transversely across the target tissue while minimizing sliding over the skin.
forceDirection: Use localized transverse loading that remains tolerable and does not provoke escalating pain.
dosage: Use short, symptom-guided bouts; progressive loading remains the main rehabilitation strategy for most tendinopathies.
steps: 1. Record the exact comparable sign for Wrist & Hand: wrist/hand range, grip, dexterity and task-related pain.
2. Screen regional red flags, contraindications and technique-specific precautions before touching the patient.
3. Position and stabilize the patient so the target is comfortable and the manual input can be localized.
4. Apply a low-force trial using the parent technique principles and the region-specific contact described above.
5. Monitor pain quality, symptom distribution, guarding and patient confidence throughout.
6. Re-test the original comparable sign immediately after the trial.
7. Keep the technique only when the response is useful, then transfer the gain into active movement, loading or self-management.
mistakes: Applying the technique because it is familiar rather than because the examination supports it.
Using more force when the response is unclear or worsening.
Failing to re-test the exact movement or function that justified the treatment.
safety: Respect fracture, acute ligament injury, inflammatory flare, nerve compression and postoperative precautions.
Stop or modify if symptoms peripheralize, neurological status worsens, the response is disproportionate or the patient asks to stop.
item.visualCue: Wrist & Hand assessment → correct regional setup → Deep Transverse Friction → immediate comparable-sign re-test.

subTechniques.name: De Quervain-Region Tendon — Deep Transverse Friction
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Selected adjunct only when the symptomatic tendon region is clearly identified and irritability is low enough to tolerate manual loading.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Sitting with forearm supported and thumb/wrist relaxed.
subTechniques.contact: Use a small precise transverse contact over the symptomatic tendon region near the radial styloid while protecting superficial sensory structures.
subTechniques.direction: Apply very small transverse movement across the tendon fibers; do not scrape along the skin.
subTechniques.dosage: Brief tolerable trial only, followed by graded thumb/wrist loading and activity modification.
subTechniques.reassess: Pain with thumb movement/grip and local tendon tenderness.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: This region is small and irritable—precision matters more than duration or force.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid acute inflammatory flare, marked swelling or sensory symptoms.
